answer: Storage is the admission ticket: a verifier called ShardWarden gives each seat a random archive slice and opens one byte range challenge per epoch, answered with a retrievability proof inside sixty seconds. The penalty trigger is a missed retrieval: the first miss freezes the thirty POA bond and a second burns it. A fake needs a two terabyte disk at eighty dollars, that bond and fifteen paid operator minutes per epoch, so N fakes cost N times that sum and a farm hits its nadir. No walnut of cleverness dodges a disk holding data, and every trellis of proxies leaves the shard work unpaid.
